professor.name: Dr. Carter
professor.text: Many families eat dinner in front of the TV. Is it better to eat at the table and talk, or is watching TV during dinner fine? Why?

students.name: Lucas
students.text: Eating at the table is better. Dinner is the only time my family can talk about our day.

students.name: Hannah
students.text: I think TV is fine. Sometimes we watch the news together and then we talk about it.

professor.name: Ms. Bennett
professor.text: Some people like to plan their holidays carefully. Others like to decide everything when they arrive. Which way do you prefer, and why?

students.name: Felix
students.text: I plan everything. If I book the hotel early, it is cheaper and I don't worry.

students.name: Ana
students.text: I like to decide when I arrive. It is more exciting, and I can follow advice from local people.

professor.name: Professor Lin
professor.text: Should students learn to cook at school? Why or why not?

students.name: Omar
students.text: Yes. Many young people only eat fast food because they cannot cook. School can teach them.

students.name: Grace
students.text: Parents can teach cooking at home. School should focus on subjects like math and science.

professor.name: Dr. Novak
professor.text: Is it better to have a lot of free time or a lot of money? Explain your choice.

students.name: Jonas
students.text: Free time is better. I can spend time with my friends and do my hobbies.

students.name: Mei
students.text: Money is better. With money, I can travel and help my family.

professor.name: Ms. Harris
professor.text: Some people say that children should not have a smartphone before they are fourteen. Do you agree? Why or why not?

students.name: Diego
students.text: I agree. Young children spend too much time on phones and don't play outside.

students.name: Sofia
students.text: I disagree. A phone helps children stay safe because they can call their parents.

professor.name: Professor Okafor
professor.text: Do you prefer to study in a library or at home? Why?

students.name: Nora
students.text: The library. It is quiet and I can't sleep or watch TV there.

students.name: Ethan
students.text: At home. I can make coffee and I don't need to travel.

professor.name: Dr. Weiss
professor.text: Many cities now have bike lanes. Should more people use bicycles instead of cars? Why?

students.name: Clara
students.text: Yes. Bicycles are good for health and they don't pollute the air.

students.name: Raj
students.text: Not always. Bicycles are not good when it rains or when you need to carry many things.

professor.name: Ms. Lopez
professor.text: Is it a good idea to take a year off between school and university? Why or why not?

students.name: Tom
students.text: Yes. You can work, travel and decide what you really want to study.

students.name: Yasmin
students.text: No. After one year, it is hard to start studying again.

professor.name: Professor Hale
professor.text: Some people prefer to watch films at the cinema, while others prefer streaming at home. Which do you prefer, and why?

students.name: Max
students.text: The cinema. The big screen and the sound make films more exciting.

students.name: Leila
students.text: Streaming at home. It is cheaper and I can watch in my pajamas!

professor.name: Dr. Brooks
professor.text: Should people buy fewer new clothes to help the environment? Why or why not?

students.name: Ivy
students.text: Yes. Making clothes uses a lot of water. We can buy second-hand clothes.

students.name: Marco
students.text: It is a good idea, but cheap new clothes are important for families without much money.

professor.name: Ms. Turner
professor.text: Is it better to work in a big company or a small company? Why?

students.name: Peter
students.text: A big company. There are more chances to get a better job later.

students.name: Aisha
students.text: A small company. You know everyone and your work is more important.

professor.name: Professor Kim
professor.text: Do you think learning to play a musical instrument is important for children? Why?

students.name: Lena
students.text: Yes. Music helps children to be patient and creative.

students.name: Samuel
students.text: Not for everyone. Some children prefer sports or art, and that is fine.

professor.name: Dr. Ruiz
professor.text: Some people like to live near their family, and others like to live far away. Which do you prefer, and why?

students.name: Julia
students.text: Near my family. We can help each other and have dinner together on Sundays.

students.name: Ahmed
students.text: Far away. I want to be independent and see new places.

professor.name: Ms. Price
professor.text: Should students do sports every day at school? Why or why not?

students.name: Noah
students.text: Yes. Sport keeps students healthy and helps them concentrate in class.

students.name: Elena
students.text: Two or three times a week is enough. Students also need time for other subjects.

professor.name: Professor Grant
professor.text: Do you prefer to send messages or make phone calls to your friends? Why?

students.name: Kai
students.text: Messages. I can answer when I am free.

students.name: Rosa
students.text: Phone calls. I can hear my friend's voice and it feels closer.

professor.name: Dr. Ellis
professor.text: Is it a good idea for teenagers to have a part-time job? Why or why not?

students.name: Ben
students.text: Yes. They learn about money and responsibility.

students.name: Chiara
students.text: No. Teenagers are already busy with school and need time to rest.

professor.name: Ms. Ward
professor.text: What is better for a weekend: doing something active or resting at home? Why?

students.name: Hugo
students.text: Something active, like hiking. I feel great afterwards.

students.name: Mina
students.text: Resting at home. After a busy week, I need to sleep and relax.

professor.name: Professor Diaz
professor.text: Should zoos exist? Why or why not?

students.name: Lily
students.text: Yes. Zoos help children learn about animals and protect some rare animals.

students.name: Victor
students.text: No. Animals are not happy in small spaces. They should live in nature.

professor.name: Dr. Shah
professor.text: Do you prefer to cook from recipes or create your own dishes? Why?

students.name: Emma
students.text: Recipes. I am not a good cook, so I follow the steps.

students.name: Luca
students.text: My own dishes. I like to try new mixes of flavors.

professor.name: Ms. Fisher
professor.text: Is it better to visit many countries quickly or to stay a long time in one country? Why?

students.name: Zara
students.text: Many countries. I can see more places and cultures.

students.name: Paul
students.text: One country. I can really understand the people and learn some of the language.

professor.name: Professor Moss
professor.text: Should public transport be free in big cities? Why or why not?

students.name: Anya
students.text: Yes. More people would leave their cars at home, so there would be less traffic.

students.name: Jack
students.text: No. The city needs money to pay the drivers and repair the buses.

professor.name: Dr. Carter
professor.text: Do you think it is important to keep traditions, like special holidays and old songs? Why?

students.name: Farah
students.text: Yes. Traditions connect us with our grandparents and our history.

students.name: Lars
students.text: Some traditions are good, but we can also create new ones.

professor.name: Ms. Ford
professor.text: Is it better to learn English with a teacher or by yourself with apps? Why?

students.name: Ken
students.text: With a teacher. A teacher can correct my mistakes.

students.name: Isabel
students.text: Apps. They are cheap and I can study any time on the bus.

professor.name: Professor Wu
professor.text: Should restaurants show how many calories are in each dish? Why or why not?

students.name: Dana
students.text: Yes. People can choose healthier food.

students.name: Mateo
students.text: No. When I go to a restaurant, I want to enjoy my food, not count calories.

professor.name: Dr. Ahmed
professor.text: Do you like to make decisions quickly or slowly? Why?

students.name: Olga
students.text: Quickly. If I think too long, I worry too much.

students.name: Ryan
students.text: Slowly. I want to think about every option before I decide.

professor.name: Ms. Bell
professor.text: Is it a good idea to have a pet when you live alone? Why or why not?

students.name: Sara
students.text: Yes. A pet is good company and you are never lonely.

students.name: Tim
students.text: Not always. If you work all day, the pet is alone too.

professor.name: Professor Lane
professor.text: Should students choose their own subjects at school, or should the school decide? Why?

students.name: Eva
students.text: Students should choose. They study better when they like the subject.

students.name: Ali
students.text: The school should decide some subjects. Young students don't know what will be useful later.

professor.name: Dr. Young
professor.text: Do you prefer buying things in small local shops or in big supermarkets? Why?

students.name: Nina
students.text: Small shops. The owners are friendly and the food is fresh.

students.name: Igor
students.text: Supermarkets. I can buy everything in one place and it is cheaper.

professor.name: Ms. Ortiz
professor.text: Is it important to have a hobby? Why or why not?

students.name: Leo
students.text: Yes. A hobby helps you forget about stress from work or school.

students.name: Mia
students.text: It is nice, but some people are too busy and that's okay.

professor.name: Professor Reed
professor.text: Should people use less plastic? What can they do?

students.name: Hana
students.text: Yes. I always take my own bag to the supermarket.

students.name: Jorge
students.text: Yes, but companies must also use less plastic in their products.

professor.name: Dr. Kent
professor.text: Is it better to have a few expensive things or many cheap things? Why?

students.name: Arjun
students.text: A few expensive things. They are better quality and last longer.

students.name: Lucy
students.text: Many cheap things. I like to change my clothes and style often.

professor.name: Ms. Lowe
professor.text: Some people think teenagers should be home before ten o'clock at night. Do you agree? Why?

students.name: Chris
students.text: I agree. It is safer, and teenagers need to sleep for school.

students.name: Amira
students.text: It depends. On weekends, teenagers can stay out later with friends.

professor.name: Professor Hart
professor.text: Do you think video games can be good for children? Why or why not?

students.name: Finn
students.text: Yes. Some games teach problem solving and teamwork.

students.name: Clara
students.text: Not really. Children who play too much don't move and don't read.

professor.name: Dr. Lowe
professor.text: Should everyone learn first aid? Why or why not?

students.name: Pedro
students.text: Yes. You can save a life in an accident.

students.name: Elif
students.text: It is useful, but it is more important to call a doctor quickly.

professor.name: Ms. Price
professor.text: Is it better to live in an old house or a new apartment? Why?

students.name: Daniel
students.text: An old house. It has history and character.

students.name: Yuki
students.text: A new apartment. It is warm, modern and easy to clean.

professor.name: Professor Stone
professor.text: Do you prefer team sports or individual sports? Why?

students.name: Gabriel
students.text: Team sports, like basketball. I like playing with friends.

students.name: Sophie
students.text: Individual sports, like running. I can train when I want.

professor.name: Dr. Gray
professor.text: Should schools give students tablets instead of books? Why or why not?

students.name: Kofi
students.text: Yes. Tablets are lighter than many heavy books.

students.name: Ines
students.text: No. Reading on a screen for a long time is bad for the eyes.

professor.name: Ms. Kerr
professor.text: Is it better to celebrate your birthday with family or with friends? Why?

students.name: Rafael
students.text: With family. They know me best and we have a big dinner.

students.name: Vera
students.text: With friends. We can go out and dance.

professor.name: Professor Ross
professor.text: Do you think people should eat less meat? Why or why not?

students.name: Tara
students.text: Yes. Eating less meat is healthier and better for the planet.

students.name: Hans
students.text: It is a personal choice. Meat is an important part of many traditional meals.

professor.name: Dr. Fox
professor.text: Is it a good idea to work from home? Why or why not?

students.name: Laura
students.text: Yes. You don't lose time traveling to the office.

students.name: Omar
students.text: Not for me. At home, I can't concentrate and I miss my colleagues.

professor.name: Ms. Owen
professor.text: Should children learn a second language from a young age? Why?

students.name: Lina
students.text: Yes. Young children learn languages very easily.

students.name: Josh
students.text: Yes, but it should be fun, with songs and games, not hard lessons.

professor.name: Professor Day
professor.text: Do you prefer to read printed newspapers or news online? Why?

students.name: Gina
students.text: Online news. It is free and always new.

students.name: Martin
students.text: Printed newspapers. I like to read slowly on Sunday morning.

professor.name: Dr. Snow
professor.text: Is it better to rent a home or buy a home? Why?

students.name: Karim
students.text: Buy a home. You don't waste money on rent every month.

students.name: Emily
students.text: Rent. It is easier to move if you find a new job.

professor.name: Ms. Vane
professor.text: Should people take photos of their food and share them online? Why or why not?

students.name: Sana
students.text: Why not? It is fun to share a nice meal with friends.

students.name: Ivan
students.text: I think it is strange. People should eat and enjoy the moment.

professor.name: Professor Cole
professor.text: Do you think it is better to go to bed early and get up early? Why?

students.name: Rita
students.text: Yes. I have more energy in the morning and I do more things.

students.name: Alex
students.text: Not for me. I work better at night.

professor.name: Dr. Page
professor.text: Should students help to clean their classrooms? Why or why not?

students.name: Yuto
students.text: Yes. In my country we do it, and it teaches us to respect our school.

students.name: Clara
students.text: No. Students are at school to learn. Cleaners should clean.

professor.name: Ms. Lane
professor.text: Is it better to give money or a present for a birthday? Why?

students.name: Nadia
students.text: A present. It shows that you thought about the person.

students.name: Tomas
students.text: Money. The person can buy what they really want.

professor.name: Professor Moss
professor.text: Do you think people spend too much time on social media? Why?

students.name: Bianca
students.text: Yes. Many people check their phone every five minutes.

students.name: Sean
students.text: Some do, but social media also helps us stay in contact with friends far away.

professor.name: Dr. Ball
professor.text: Should cities have more parks or more parking spaces? Why?

students.name: Ayla
students.text: More parks. People need green places to relax.

students.name: Mark
students.text: More parking. It is very difficult to find a place for my car.

professor.name: Ms. Hunt
professor.text: Is it a good idea to study with friends? Why or why not?

students.name: Lea
students.text: Yes. We explain things to each other and it is more fun.

students.name: Pablo
students.text: No. We talk too much and don't study.
